title: FedCF: Fair Federated Conformal Prediction
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A federated model's conformal predictions are audited and iteratively corrected through client-server threshold exchange until fairness-conditional coverage holds across groups.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right server flow, clients below with feedback loop arrows
description: A single wide diagram with a dashed blue Server region on top and a dashed Clients region at the bottom left. The server flow runs left to right through rounded gray boxes. First is a Federated ML Model, drawn as a neural network. Next is Federated Conformal Prediction, with a coverage interval bar and a bar chart for groups g_a, g_b and g_c. This box is marked 'Fairness Conditional Coverage Violated' with a red X. Arrows labeled 'Local Coverage Statistics' go up to the server, and 'New Thresholds' arrows go back down to the clients. Red and green marks give the contrast.
caption: End-to-End FedCF Pipeline.
abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) is a widely used technique for quantifying uncertainty in machine learning models. In its standard form, CP offers probabilistic guarantees on the coverage of the true label, but it is agnostic to sensitive attributes in the dataset. Several recent works have sought to incorporate fairness into CP by ensuring conditional coverage guarantees across different subgroups. One such method is Conformal Fairness (CF). In this work, we extend the CF framework to the Federated Learning setting and discuss how we can audit a federated model for fairness by analyzing the fairness-related gaps for different demographic groups. We empirically validate our framework by conducting experiments on several datasets spanning multiple domains, fully leveraging the exchangeability assumption.
